concepts.why: The patient's biopsy results showed lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis, consistent with invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
Dermoscopic evaluation of the papules revealed features typical of basal cell carcinoma.
The patient presented with a crusty lesion in the right fronto-orbital region, which could be a precursor to actinic keratosis.
The patient's lesion had a similar appearance to keratoacanthoma, although the biopsy results were more consistent with invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

The patient's biopsy results showed pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli, which could be consistent with Bowen's disease, although the presence of invasive features makes invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma more likely.
The patient's lesion had a similar appearance to seborrheic keratosis, although the biopsy results were more consistent with invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
The patient's lesion had a similar appearance to dermatofibroma, although the biopsy results were more consistent with invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

The patient's biopsy results showed pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli, which could be consistent with squamous cell carcinoma in situ, although the presence of invasive features makes invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma more likely.

rationales.F05: Eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli are characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma.
rationales.F07: The diagnosis of invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma was directly stated.
rationales.F11: The presence of features typical of basal cell carcinoma rules out other diagnoses.

frontier_selector.rationale: The biopsy results showing lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis, along with the initial PET/CT uptake and subsequent regression of the plaque, strongly support Invasive Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma as the primary diagnosis, while the appearance of discrete papular lesions with features typical of basal cell carcinoma suggests a possible secondary or concurrent diagnosis.
